title: Per-model kernel profiles and compilation hinting for heterogeneous-attention architectures (MHA/GQA/MoE)
creator: Lucas Nguyen
description:
Problem: Our current model onboarding flow picks kernels with a single global policy. Heterogeneous-attention models (multi-headed attention, grouped-qa/GQA, and mixture-of-experts) show divergent microbenchmark characteristics: some layers benefit from fused MHA kernels, others from shard-aware kernels, and MoE routers require different compilation flags to avoid OOM and improve latency tail. Without per-model hints, we see 10-30% tail-latency regressions and multiple emergency rollbacks during recent onboards.

Goal: Add a first-class, per-model kernel profile and compilation-hinting mechanism that: (1) allows the model-onboarder to publish an immutable kernel_profile_id for a model+version, (2) supports multiple profile tiers (aggressive / balanced / conservative / fallback), (3) is consumable by the compiler/runtime at load time to select kernel variants and compile flags, and (4) integrates with the existing rollout/canary system so we can A/B profile choices.

Scope:
- Implement a kernel_profile manifest (JSON) definition and storage in the model-onboarder datastore.
- Extend the onboarding CLI and web UI to capture recommended profile (including quantization hint, preferred kernel family, fused-op preference, per-layer overrides for routing/experts).
- Add runtime hooks to: look up model+version -> kernel_profile_id, validate compatibility with runtime hardware, and apply compile-time hints (e.g., prefer fused MHA, enable group GEMM kernels, set KV-cache allocation targets).
- Create an autotune CI job that runs representative microbenchmarks (latency P50/P95/P99, memory) and proposes a recommended profile.

Out of scope:
- Automatic live re-compilation in production (we will rely on staged rollouts and new deployments).
- New kernel implementations (we're only choosing among existing kernels and flags).

Acceptance criteria:
- A kernel_profile JSON schema and storage path exist and are immutable once published for a model+version.
- Onboarder UI/CLI can attach a profile_id to an onboarding artifact and publish to the catalog.
- Runtime can fetch and apply the profile on model load; telemetry shows the selected kernel family in traces.
- CI autotune job produces a recommended profile and stores the benchmark artifact as an attachment.
- One canary rollout is completed for the internal GQA benchmark with the "balanced" profile showing <=5% P95 regression vs baseline.

Risks and mitigations:
- Mismatch between profile and deployed hardware: implement a validation step that marks profiles incompatible if required kernels are not compiled for that GPU type.
- Profile proliferation: introduce a lifecycle policy (expire profiles after 12 months, mark superseded ones).

Implementation notes / design decisions:
- Profile format: small JSON with fields: profile_id, model_version, tier (aggressive|balanced|conservative|fallback), kernel_preferences (ordered list), per_layer_overrides (list of layer glob patterns -> hint map), compile_flags, expected_memory_footprint_estimate. Keep schema intentionally flat and string-keyed for easy indexing.
- Pinning policy: model-onboarder will publish model_version -> kernel_profile_id mapping into the catalog. Releases will reference model_version; rollback uses the previous model_version/profile.
- Canary flow: the rollout controller will accept a profile_id override at rollout-start to perform profile A/B testing.

Notes for reviewers:
- We considered a binary blob for profiles (faster lookup) but chose JSON for debuggability and traceability.
- We will add a small metrics label "kernel_profile_id" to request traces for post-rollout comparison.

Next steps (engineering tasks):
1) Define JSON schema and add storage API (ENG-27644-1).
2) Add onboarding CLI/UI fields and validation (ENG-27644-2).
3) Implement runtime lookup & apply hooks (ENG-27644-3).
4) CI autotune job + benchmark harness integration (ENG-27644-4).
5) Canary automation and dashboard filters (ENG-27644-5).
